name: Learn proper throwing mechanics for a baseball
blurb: Good throwing mechanics protect your arm as much as they add velocity: the sequence runs legs, hips, torso, shoulder, elbow, hand, and skipping any link costs you both.
gear: A partner or a wall, and space
steps: Learn the four-seam grip: two fingers across the seams with a small gap under the ball, for straight true flight.
Warm up properly with short, easy throws before anything hard. Cold arms are how elbows get hurt.
Learn the sequence with a shuffle: glove side leads, front shoulder points at the target, hips open first, then torso, then the arm whips through.
Keep the throwing elbow at or above shoulder height — dropping it is the classic injury pattern.
Finish with the throwing shoulder pulling down and across the opposite knee.
Practise long toss to build arm strength gradually, then come back in to short accurate throws.
tips: All-arm throwing hurts and is slow. If your legs are not tired, you are not using them.
Never throw hard without a full warm-up, and stop at the first sign of elbow pain.
proof: Accurate, comfortable throws at 40 metres with a full-body sequence and no arm soreness afterwards.
